Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  November 2, 2023

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on November 2, 2023. Commissioner
Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Cynthia
  McLemore - District 3, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner
  at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Octavio Padilla - District 2, Commissioner Christopher
  Beck - District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director
  Craig Civitello  Lead Park Maintenance Worker
  Geoffrey Okamoto  H.S. Transportation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Mary Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS. VERBAL REPORTS

PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Lead Park Maintenance Worker, Craig Civitello reported the
following: GRAFFITI DIVISION - there has been an increase in gang graffiti around
Manchester and Crenshaw area, also in District 4 on Yukon, Doty and Lemoli Avenues. The
Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739. PARKS DIVISION - we are performing our regular duties.
With the increase in traffic due to the events at SoFi Stadium and at The Forum, the litter
we are picking up in our center medians has increased, mostly along Century Avenue and
Manchester Boulevard. Contractors are starting to prepare to install the new walking track
at Darby Park. Currently the irrigation is off at the park. The new pump track at Vincent
Park is a hit and is used every day.

REPORTS - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Mary Rouzan reported the following:
CULTURAL OFFERINGS - the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department hosts

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

several classes and activities for youth, adults and senior citizens. I encourage you all to
take a look at the Fall/Winter Community Information Guide. The guide outlines all the
department offerings, including information on how to register for the classes. TURKEY
GIVEAWAY- the City of Inglewood’s Annual Turkey Giveaway Presented by Pepsi and Don
Lee Farms will take place on Tuesday, November 21, from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at Hollywood
Park. The event will serve 2,500 Inglewood residents, providing turkeys donated by Don
Lee Farms, a bag of sides, and additional items from Pepsi. This is a drive-thru event and
participants must be registered in advance to receive the items. No walk-ups are allowed.
To register, call the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department at (310) 412-
8750. HOLIDAY TREE LIGHTING CEREMONY- Please join us for this year’s “Light Up Market
Street” Holiday Fair & Tree Lighting Ceremony on Friday, December 1 from 4:00 – 8:00
p.m. in downtown Inglewood on Market Street. Please note this is a new location. We
invite you all to attend this special event that marks the beginning of the holiday season.
There will be live entertainment, refreshments, and a special visit from SANTA! New this
year, the event will also include a snow play area, roller-skating rink, food trucks,
community organizations, and more. The entire community is encouraged to attend this
festive holiday event. SPORTS - For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports
Leagues, visit our city sports website at: https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Transportation Supervisor, Geoffrey
Okamoto reported the following: SENIOR CENTER ACTIVITIES AND PROGRAMS - the
senior center continues to increase in popularity, and October saw our wonderful
Halloween party take place on Tuesday, October 31st. We are in the beginning stages of
expanding the programs and activities we offer, with staff gathering information on classes
and activities from senior centers all over the region. We will be working closely with our
Inglewood Senior Center Advisory Committee to bring more valuable resources and
programming to our Senior Center than ever before. NUTRITION - we are serving
approximately 450 seniors per week through home delivered meals for homebound
seniors and congregate lunches at our Senior Center. We continue to provide fresh
produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute. We are have
been working with our seniors to develop new menus for the next year and are looking
forward to many new and exciting additions to our menu, including a special Juneteenth
meal. SENIOR TRANSPORTATION - our paratransit program continues to provide trips to
seniors. The I-Line starts at the Inglewood Senior Center; operates Monday through Friday
from 10am to 12pm and 1pm to 5pm and takes an hour to make one full loop of all its
stops. The Trolley is free to the public. If the public wanted the I-Line’s whereabouts during
the day, they can contact the dispatch office at 310.412.4378. We also provided
transportation for seniors to our City’s Dia De Los Muertos event on Saturday, October 28.
CHILD AND ADULT CARE FOOD PROGRAM (CACFP) - the Child and Adult Care Food
Program (CACFP) serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at Crenshaw
Library, Inglewood Main Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park. The program's hours are

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snacks from 4:30
PM - 5:00 PM. We serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks per week.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. None

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Jose Palomares, District 3 Commissioner and a 45-year resident
whom is very involved in the city and runs soccer programs in Santa Monica and at Edward
Vincent Park where he has 250 kids. He stated there are some palm trees and other trees
at Edward Vincent Park that need to be trimmed. Mr. Palomares suggested a walk through
the park to determine how to spend funds and make the park safer. Another suggestion
he had is adding speed bumps to the parking lot located next to Champions Field.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown informed the Commission that the El
Segundo Little League won the American Legion Baseball State Championship and will give
the Director information on how to start a League in the city.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:37 p.m.
